findings.summary: Does DotF16 hold when a subnormal float16 operand sets the wgmma window (L125's mechanism)? This kernel's ppT and dsT are often subnormal float16
findings.detail: Round 24 found (L125; num.md, the fp8 bullet of the chunk model and 'Device questions') that on wgmma the window is set by exponent fields, and that a subnormal fp8 operand's field reads as the smallest normal's. num.md's 16-bit bullet derives DotF16 from 'every term down to at least 2^-23 of the largest', and evidence/num-dot's new note says its Part 2 had no input where a product with a subnormal operand sets the window. If float16 wgmma aligns the same way, a product with a subnormal operand (2^-24, read as 2^-14) can set the unit 10 binades too high. The other products just below that unit are then lost, far beyond relDot16 K of the magnitude sum. This kernel feeds such operands to DotF16 in its real use: ppT = fp16(P) and dsT = fp16(dS) (lines 302, 309, 355) are subnormal whenever |P| or |dS| < 2^-14, which is frequent at N_CTX = 2^14 with the benchmark's sharp softmax; q and arg_k have subnormal elements too. On the host's inputs the possible loss is tiny next to Post's per-pair 2^-25 floors, but the proof cites DotF16 as stated. Same question as grouped_matmul_tma_f16#F5 (REPORTS.md); filed here so that this kernel's exposure is on record. Not blocking: I carry on as if the library were right.
